title: Twisted three-place worlds: when a twist is defined, hidden, frozen or forced to wind
claim: For fair contacts with a visible bit and three hidden places on a triangulated surface, a twist (a cocycle flipping the hidden places' polarities relative to each triangle's first corner) changes the random world only through its cohomology class exactly when the contact is complement-closed (flipping all three places exchanges its two relations); otherwise a contractible seam is a physical defect. Independent fair polarities make every twist invisible, and two hidden places give a two-literal world. The monotone contact from four-place not-all-equal contradicts in a twist only if the cubic dual graph has no 2-factor in the class dual to the twist; on every triangular torus with sides 2 to 5 it never contradicts in any twist (by such a 2-factor except on four non-simplicial two-row tori, where every x was enumerated), so that world is frozen there. For a complement-closed contact whose doubly allowed patterns tile the plane, planar patches and fitting twists never contradict, and on a torus every minimal contradicting set of triangles winds, along a period lattice on which the twist differs from every fitting twist (a line runs along a class that the relative twist makes odd), so a lone winding contradiction event is well defined.
failure_conditions: A complement-closed instance whose seam-moved or corner-changed world is not equisatisfiable after the flip of x.

A twisted not-all-equal colouring whose cocycle has a triangle without exactly two ones or whose class differs from the twist, or a contradiction of the monotone world on a triangular torus with sides 2 to 5.

A placement with a doubly allowed assignment that contradicts on a planar patch or in a fitting twist, or a minimal contradicting set with zero winding or with a lattice on which the twist agrees with some fitting twist.
foundation_claim_scope: Random constraint worlds of fair three-place contacts on triangulated surfaces; exact statements about twists, frozen worlds and winding contradictions. Lattices are declared; no space or physics is claimed.

validation.status: checked: prose proof; check.py (standard library, own solver) confirms Lemma 1 on 240 random instances (seam moves and first-corner changes equisatisfiable after the flip of x) and its converse over all 65,536 contact pairs, Lemma 2 on 120 instances, Lemma 3 on all relations on two bits; Proposition 4 on the 3 x 3 and 4 x 4 tori (196 colourings, cocycle and class as stated) and on all triangular tori with sides 2 to 5 and every shear (220 of 224 shape-twist pairs have a twisted not-all-equal colouring; on the other four, two-row tori with shear 1, every x was enumerated and none contradicts); Theorem 5 on all 54 tiling placements (no planar or fitting-twist contradiction; 306 of 306 minimal contradicting sets wind, on lattices where the twist differs from every fitting twist). Two controls rejected. A first statement of Proposition 4 (colourings in every twist) was false and is corrected. No human or external review
validation.level: V1 prose proof with sampled checks
